newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamists reject call for new alliance deal.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamists reject call for new alliance deal.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist senior coalition partners on Monday rejected a thinly veiled offer from the main opposition party to form a new government if the ruling alliance crumbled in a security scandal.

"When there is a government, and it is working, none of the coalition partners will try to form a new government," leading Welfare Party MP Oguzhan Asilturk told a news conference. "That would be unnatural, unacceptable behaviour."
Shares on the Istanbul stock exchange fell 1.46 percent in morning trading on fears of political instability, brokers said. They recovered later.

Opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) leader Mesut Yilmaz said last week he would be open to any new formula to form a government if the present coalition collapsed over allegations of links between state officials and far-right gangsters.
His remarks were seen as a nod to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare to break its coalition with the conservative True Path Party and join ANAP in a new government.
The True Path, led by Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, has taken the brunt of criticism in the scandal.
A True Path MP was quizzed by a prosecutor last week and a close Ciller aide resigned as interior minister last month as part of the security row.
